name: The Rival Mob
label: Revelation
lede: A Boston band built from a dozen other Boston bands, fronted by Mind Eraser's drummer, playing 1989 New York hardcore like nobody had told them it was over.

eras.title: NYC meets Boston meets Cleveland, 1989
eras.text: Brendan Radigan, who drummed in the powerviolence band Mind Eraser, and Justin DeTore started The Rival Mob to play late-'80s hardcore straight: Breakdown, Rest in Pieces, Youth of Today, Warzone. Two 7"s on small labels made them the Boston band people on the hardcore message boards were talking about.

q: NYC meets BOSTON meets CLEVO in 1989.
years.h: Brendan Radigan and Justin DeTore start The Rival Mob
years.p: Radigan sings rather than drums this time. Members come from Mind Eraser, Righteous Jams, Mental, XfilesX and more, and the band's first demo comes out the same year.
Recorded and mixed by Chris Corry at the Pain Cave. The first press is 700 on black, and the B-side covers fellow Boston hardcore band Down But Not Out.

years.h: Hardcore for Hardcore 7" · Six Feet Under Records
years.p: Six songs. ALARM's reviewer heard heaviness built from switches of emphasis and syncopation, not chugging, and compared the effect to Sepultura and Black Flag.

eras.title: Caveman steroids
eras.text: Revelation, the label that had put out the New York records The Rival Mob were chasing, signed them for their first album.

years.h: The Rival Mob sign to Revelation Records
years.p: Revelation's announcement promised the Rival Mob formula pumped full of caveman steroids, and a record not for the faint of heart or the faint of pit.

years.h: Full set filmed by hate5six, August 11, 2012
yt: Full set filmed by hate5six, August 11, 2012

years.src: Discogs · Revelation Records pressing history · Legends Arising · Hardcore Punk Wiki
years.p: Twelve songs, from Intro Grunt to Thought Control, recorded and mixed by guitarist Trevor Vaughan. Revelation's first run is 1,095 on gold, 655 on black and 438 on seafoam green.
years.xp: The line-up on the record: Brendan Radigan on vocals, Trevor Vaughan and Doug Free on guitars, Pearse McGrath on bass. Legends Arising made it its album of the month for March 2013. A 2023 rundown of the Revelation catalog called it a love letter to the old Boston hardcore scene.

eras.title: We never break up
eras.text: The Rival Mob kept turning up at the big hardcore festivals (This Is Hardcore, Sound and Fury, Chaos in Tejas) and made a first trip to Europe. But Brendan Radigan had a day job and several other bands, and the new 7" never came out.

years.h: The Rival Mob play Black N' Blue Bowl at Webster Hall
years.p: Fresh back from Sweden, The Rival Mob play New York's Black N' Blue Bowl, with This Is Hardcore booked too and a new 7" written but unrecorded.

years.h: Brendan Radigan on The Rival Mob's future
years.p: Radigan told Vice The Rival Mob don't break up, they just go quiet. He was also singing or drumming in Mind Eraser, Battle Ruins, Stone Dagger and [[Magic Circle|688fe3f7-3a4c-4fb9-bca8-f5ee213fa710]].

eras.title: A picture disc and a gold record
eras.text: No new songs, but Mob Justice kept selling. Revelation kept pressing it, in formats the label almost never uses.

years.h: Mob Justice becomes Revelation's third-ever picture disc
years.p: A picture disc pressing of Mob Justice, according to Hardcore Punk Wiki only the third in Revelation's history.

years.h: Mob Justice back again, on goldenrod vinyl
years.p: A limited goldenrod reissue of Mob Justice is listed, thirteen years after the album first came out.
